display: French sommelier at a Bund restaurant in Shanghai for nine years, learning Chinese, and always up for a good glass and a Thursday football match.

signals.text: I'm refreshing our Christmas wine list and want to bring in a few small Loire and Jura producers without raising the average bottle price.
I taste with importers twice a week and I'm looking for small, story-rich producers that Shanghai guests will remember.
My Chinese is stuck at around 600 characters and I want a practice partner or a better method to get past the plateau.
I want to read Chinese books with my kids, but my 12-year-old already reads faster than I do.
I play five-a-side football on Thursday evenings and enjoy it, though my knee complains.
My kids' international school is raising fees by 20 percent, and I'm weighing a local bilingual school in Pudong that I know nothing about.
I need someone who can tell me what a local bilingual school is really like day to day: the rigor, the maths, the pressure, and how foreign kids settle in.
The Pudong school has an open day on 17 October, mostly in Chinese, and I need someone to come along and translate.
I'd like to talk to parents who have moved their kids from an international school to a local bilingual one, and hear what they'd do differently.
I worry that changing schools will cost my kids their friends, and I don't know how to soften that.
The school deposit is due on 7 November, so I need a decision framework that will get me to a decision, not another month of thinking.
My lower back hurts from carrying cases up the cellar stairs, and I haven't done anything about it yet.
I tend to postpone big decisions, and at home the pressure to settle the school question is building.

offers.text: I can build or refresh a restaurant wine list of 600 labels or fewer, balancing margin, story and guest taste, with nine years of Shanghai experience.
I can set up cellar management: inventory, rotation, temperature control and supplier negotiation.
I hold the Court of Master Sommeliers advanced certificate and can run a small tasting or food-pairing session, in French or English.
I know importers and merchants in Shanghai, Hong Kong and Bordeaux and can introduce small producers to the right buyers.
I can advise a small producer on how to tell a story that works with Shanghai restaurant guests rather than just push a label.
I speak native French and fluent English, so I can offer French conversation practice, perhaps in exchange for Mandarin practice.
I can pour wine for a private dinner or corporate evening, though only on weekdays outside my restaurant shifts.
I can give a new arrival in Shanghai's hospitality trade an honest picture of how an expat sommelier career works here.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I make natural wine in the Jura, about 15,000 bottles a year, and I'm looking for a first foothold in Shanghai restaurants.
catchers.can: Taste the wines and, if they fit, put them on the list or introduce the producer to importers I trust.
catchers.confirm: Are the wines already available through a licensed importer or distributor in China, or can you set that up?

catchers.hypo: I'm opening a restaurant in Shanghai and have no idea how to build a wine list that makes money.
catchers.can: Share how I structure a list by price tier, margin and story, and review a draft list.
catchers.confirm: Is this a restaurant that will serve food in a sit-down setting, rather than a bar or retail shop?

catchers.hypo: My child goes to the local bilingual school in Pudong, and I'm happy to tell another parent what it's like.
catchers.can: Listen and ask my questions, and offer something in return, such as wine advice or French conversation practice.
catchers.confirm: Does your child currently attend that school, or one very like it, rather than only having heard about it?

catchers.hypo: I'm a Chinese-English speaker and I'd happily go through a school open day with a foreign parent.
catchers.can: Go with me to the 17 October open day, and I'd buy lunch and answer your questions about wine in return.
catchers.confirm: Are you free on Saturday, 17 October, and able to interpret live, not just translate documents?

catchers.hypo: I teach Chinese characters to adults who are stuck at the intermediate stage.
catchers.can: Try your method on my 600-character plateau and tell my teacher what worked.
catchers.confirm: Do you work with adult learners in Shanghai, either in person or online, in the evenings or on weekdays?

catchers.hypo: My wife's colleague is a local sommelier who wants to move from Chinese to international restaurants.
catchers.can: Through my friend Wei, a local sommelier, I can offer an introduction to the trade and honest advice on certification.
catchers.confirm: Is the person already working in wine service, rather than only interested in wine as a hobby?

catchers.hypo: I'm a consultant helping an expat family choose between international and local schools, and I'd like to speak to a parent who has weighed it.
catchers.can: Through my wife Claire, who works in consulting, I can pass on the request, and I can share my own decision criteria.
catchers.confirm: Is your question about education choices for expat families in Shanghai, not about visas or relocation?

catchers.hypo: I run a Thursday-night five-a-side game in Shanghai and need a reliable player.
catchers.can: Join, since Thursday is already my football night, and bring a friend if there is space.
catchers.confirm: Is the game played on Thursday evenings, in a language mix that includes English or French?

catchers.hypo: I'm a physiotherapist or sports-medicine doctor in Shanghai who treats people with manual-handling back pain.
catchers.can: Book an appointment, and in return offer a wine tasting for your team.
catchers.confirm: Do you see English- or French-speaking patients, and can you take new patients within a few weeks?

forbids.text: I will not move my kids to a school I have not visited myself.
I cannot take meetings on weekday evenings, because those are my working hours.
Weekends are for family, so I only take work calls and events then in exceptional cases.
I won't push a label onto my list at a price I can't justify to guests, whatever the supplier says.
I won't discuss the value of my private wine collection or my personal finances.
The school decision cannot be postponed beyond November.

projects.name: Christmas wine list 2026
projects.text: Refresh the restaurant's wine list by the end of October for a 15 December launch, adding small Loire and Jura producers while keeping margins and the average bottle price steady.
roles_needed: small-producer or importer with Loire/Jura wines
graphic designer for the wine list

projects.name: School decision
projects.text: Decide between my kids' international school and a local bilingual school in Pudong before the 7 November deposit deadline, after visiting the school on 17 October.
roles_needed: parent of a pupil at a local bilingual school
Chinese-English interpreter for the open day

policy.t1: When there is a real lead, I'll share the school-fee question, the Pudong bilingual school I'm considering, the open-day date, and my wine-list needs and contacts.
policy.t2: Once I trust the other party, I'll share my back pain, family pressure around the school decision, and the worry about my kids' friendships.
policy.never: The value of my wine collection and any details of my personal finances or savings.
